messages.subject: Re: leaflet-shiny & heatmap
parts:
I use the leaflet class in rCharts. 
I have modified some files of rCharts. 

The main idea is to pass the data to shiny-server:
m <- Leaflet$new()

  Points <- as.list(rep(NA, nrow(post)))
      for (i in 1:nrow(post)) {
        Points[[i]] <- c(lat = post$Lat[i], lon = post$Long[i], value = sample(1:10, 1))
      }
      
m$addParams(heatmap = Points)


Then the data will appear in your web browser, so you can add some JavaScript in ui.r to render the data to heatmap.

Hi HuiDong

I am a bit confused.  First, if I understand this correctly, you didn't used shiny-leaflet package but rCharts (obviously both based on leaflet library).

Your code example does not exactly clarify how to do the heat map.  I have used the code below (object also of a stack overflow question still unanswered!).

Main issue is that I do not know how to reset the heat map layer in shiny (I can do it in a normal R code).  After the first heat map, all the others are piled up on top of the first.

Would you be so kind to comment on my code please, or possibly show me the code you have used for the heath map? Thanks

library(shiny)
library(rCharts)
library(rjson)
library(data.table)
##   
crimedt <- as.data.table(na.omit(ggmap::crime[,c("address","offense","lon","lat")]))
crimedt <- crimedt[,offense:=as.character(offense)]
setkey(crimedt, lat,lon,offense)
crime_cdt <- crimedt[, .(count = length(address))
                          , by = .(lat,lon,offense)]
setkey(crime_cdt,offense)
seLabels <- unique(crime_cdt$offense)

#
runApp(list(
  ui =   tabPanel("main", fluidPage(
    h4("Crime hotmap"),
    column(3,
    selectInput("slCrime", "Choose Crime Type:",
                                            seLabels, seLabels[1])
    ),
    column(9,
           chartOutput('baseMap','leaflet'),
           tags$style('.leaflet {height: 500px;}'),
           tags$head(tags$script(src="http://leaflet.github.io/Leaflet.heat/dist/leaflet-heat.js"))
            , uiOutput('datamap')
    )
  )),
server = function(input, output, session) {
output$baseMap<-renderMap({
baseMap <- Leaflet$new()
mlon <- mean(crime_cdt$lon)
mlat <- mean(crime_cdt$lat)
baseMap$setView(c(mlat,mlon),9)
baseMap$tileLayer(provider="OpenStreetMap")
baseMap
 })
output$datamap<-renderUI({ 
    if(is.null(input$slCrime)) { return() }
    q = quote(input$slCrime)
    crime_cdt <- crime_cdt[eval(q), .(lat, lon, count)]
    maxdat <- max(crime_cdt$count)
  arrdat <- toJSONArray2(crime_cdt, json=F, names=F)
  jsdat <- rjson::toJSON(arrdat)

tags$body(tags$script(HTML(sprintf("
var addressPoints = %s
var maxval = %f
var heat = L.heatLayer(addressPoints, {maxZoom: 9, radius: 20, blur: 40}).addTo(map)
 </script>",  jsdat, maxdat
))))
})
}
))

On Wednesday, November 12, 2014 10:59:34 PM UTC+1, Enzo wrote:
Hi HuiDong

I am a bit confused.  First, if I understand this correctly, you didn't used shiny-leaflet package but rCharts (obviously both based on leaflet library).

Your code example does not exactly clarify how to do the heat map.  I have used the code below (object also of a stack overflow question still unanswered!).

Main issue is that I do not know how to reset the heat map layer in shiny (I can do it in a normal R code).  After the first heat map, all the others are piled up on top of the first.

Would you be so kind to comment on my code please, or possibly show me the code you have used for the heath map? Thanks

library(shiny)
library(rCharts)
library(rjson)
library(data.table)
##   
crimedt <- as.data.table(na.omit(ggmap::crime[,c("address","offense","lon","lat")]))
crimedt <- crimedt[,offense:=as.character(offense)]
setkey(crimedt, lat,lon,offense)
crime_cdt <- crimedt[, .(count = length(address))
                          , by = .(lat,lon,offense)]
setkey(crime_cdt,offense)
seLabels <- unique(crime_cdt$offense)

#
runApp(list(
  ui =   tabPanel("main", fluidPage(
    h4("Crime hotmap"),
    column(3,
    selectInput("slCrime", "Choose Crime Type:",
                                            seLabels, seLabels[1])
    ),
    column(9,
           chartOutput('baseMap','leaflet'),
           tags$style('.leaflet {height: 500px;}'),
           tags$head(tags$script(src="http://leaflet.github.io/Leaflet.heat/dist/leaflet-heat.js"))
            , uiOutput('datamap')
    )
  )),
server = function(input, output, session) {
output$baseMap<-renderMap({
baseMap <- Leaflet$new()
mlon <- mean(crime_cdt$lon)
mlat <- mean(crime_cdt$lat)
baseMap$setView(c(mlat,mlon),9)
baseMap$tileLayer(provider="OpenStreetMap")
baseMap
 })
output$datamap<-renderUI({ 
    if(is.null(input$slCrime)) { return() }
    q = quote(input$slCrime)
    crime_cdt <- crime_cdt[eval(q), .(lat, lon, count)]
    maxdat <- max(crime_cdt$count)
  arrdat <- toJSONArray2(crime_cdt, json=F, names=F)
  jsdat <- rjson::toJSON(arrdat)

tags$body(tags$script(HTML(sprintf("
var addressPoints = %s
var maxval = %f
var heat = L.heatLayer(addressPoints, {maxZoom: 9, radius: 20, blur: 40}).addTo(map)
 </script>",  jsdat, maxdat
))))
})
}
))

Hi again,
  I wrote a demo for this thread. 

## ui.R
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
    tagList(
      tags$body(
        tags$script(src="heatmap.js"),
        tags$script(src="heatmap-leaflet.js")
      )
    ),
    sliderInput("num", "Case number",
                50, 300, 100, step = 1),
  showOutput("myMap", "leaflet")
))


## server.R
library(shiny)
library(rCharts)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  output$myMap <- renderMap({
    m <- Leaflet$new()
    m$setView(c(30, 105), zoom = 4)
    m$addParams(width="100%", height = "800", layerOpts = "",
                urlTemplate= 'http://{s}.tile3.opencyclemap.org/landscape/{z}/{x}/{y}.png')
    dat <- expand.grid(lon = seq(95, 115), lat = seq(20, 40))
    dat$value <- runif(nrow(dat))
    dat <- dat[sample(seq(nrow(dat)), input$num), ]
    Points <- as.list(rep(NA, nrow(dat)))
    for (i in 1:nrow(dat)) {
      Points[[i]] <- c(lat = dat$lat[i], lon = dat$lon[i], value = dat$value[i])
    }
    m$addParams(heatmap = Points)
    m
  })
})


## Important !!
Include the following script to the end of "~\R\win-library\3.0\rCharts\libraries\leaflet\layouts\chart.html"

if (spec.heatmap != undefined) {
var heatmapLayer = L.TileLayer.heatMap({
radius: 20,
opacity: 0.8,
gradient: {
0.45: "rgb(0,0,255)",
0.55: "rgb(0,255,255)",
0.65: "rgb(0,255,0)",
0.95: "yellow",
1.00: "rgb(255,0,0)"
}
});
heatmapLayer.addData(spec.heatmap);
map.addLayer(heatmapLayer);
  }


##  You need to download the two JavaScript librares in ui.R and put them into folder call 'www' under your project folder.

I use the leaflet class in rCharts. 
I have modified some files of rCharts. 

The main idea is to pass the data to shiny-server:
m <- Leaflet$new()

  Points <- as.list(rep(NA, nrow(post)))
      for (i in 1:nrow(post)) {
        Points[[i]] <- c(lat = post$Lat[i], lon = post$Long[i], value = sample(1:10, 1))
      }
      
m$addParams(heatmap = Points)


Then the data will appear in your web browser, so you can add some JavaScript in ui.r to render the data to heatmap.
